lines.text: Welcome to The Calm Cash Show.
Today is a short one about one habit that changes your whole month.
When do you send the first invoice?
Most studios I work with send it when the project ends.
That feels fair.
You did the work, now you bill for it.
Here's what that costs you.
Say the project runs four weeks.
You invoice at the end on net 30.
Your client pays a little late, like most clients do.
That's about 60 days between the first day of work and the money in your account.
For those 60 days you're paying your team, your rent, your software.
You're lending your client the whole project for free.
So here's what I teach.
Send the invoice the day the work starts.
A third to start, a third at the midpoint, a third on delivery.
I call it the three-payment split.
Put it in the proposal, in the price section, before anyone signs.
Then it isn't a surprise.
It's just how you work.
One of my clients, Priya, runs a video studio.
She used to wait about 60 days on every project.
Now new projects pay the first third within a week of kickoff.
She told me payroll Friday is boring now.
That's the goal.
If you want the template I use, the proposal wording and the three invoices, comment SPLIT and I'll send it to you.
